entries.zh: 乏善可陈的更新
entries.en: Lackluster Update

entries.zh: 我们十分抱歉，来自[Root.GetRulerName]的赞助人：我们很不幸陷入了创作的瓶颈期。整个城邦目前还处于紊乱的状态，尚不能提供任何成果。一如既往，我们仍然十分感谢您的赞助。
entries.en: We apologize, patron [Root.GetRulerName]: we have sadly reached something of a creative roadblock. The enclave is in disarray and we have nothing to offer at this time. We thank you for your patronage, as always.

entries.zh: 希望状况能有所改善。
entries.en: We hope the situation improves.

entries.zh: 我们要求退款！
entries.en: We demand a refund!

entries.zh: 破碎的艺术
entries.en: Broken Artistry

entries.zh: 您好，来自[Root.GetRulerName]的赞助人。由于一个重大故障，我们最近不得不报废掉大多数的技术设备。您是否能用得上其中所产生的零件或原料呢？
entries.en: Greetings, patron [Root.GetRulerName]. We have recently been forced to scrap most of our technical equipment due to a major malfunction. Would the materials and scrap be of any use to you, by any chance?

entries.zh: 我们会回收原料的。
entries.en: We will salvage the materials.

entries.zh: 我们会帮助你们修理的。
entries.en: We will repair it for you.

entries.zh: 赞助者，我们听到这个消息真是出离地抱歉！没有时事通讯，我们就无法向你传达我们最近的成果……
entries.en: We are exceptionally sorry to hear that, o patron! Without the newsletter we won't be able to keep you up-to-date on our latest accomplishments...

entries.zh: 文化中心
entries.en: The Ministry of Culture

entries.zh: 啊，§Y文化中心§!……它的任务就是挑战与常理背道而驰的观念，提升你帝国内艺术的凝聚力。让我来说，完全就是一个杰作。
entries.en: Ah, the §YMinistry of Culture§!... It was designed to challenge divergent ideas and promote greater unity throughout your empire through the medium of art. A true masterpiece, if I may say so myself.

entries.zh: 很好！这件杰作很快就会被送到您的贮藏设施中。只需要让你的工人们建到任何你自己的行星即可。\n我们由衷感谢您的赞助。
entries.en: Excellent! The piece will be sent to your storage facility immediately. Simply ask your builders to erect it on any planet you wish.\nWe humbly thank you for your patronage.

entries.zh: 我们从艺术家联盟收到了一条信息。他们的一座空间站被摧毁了！
entries.en: We have received a transmission from the Artisan Troupe. One of their stations has been destroyed!

entries.zh: 我们收到了一条来自艺术家联盟首席的绝望的求救信息。他们的最后一个空间站与他们的文化都被毁灭殆尽。几乎没有幸存者留下来，艺术家联盟已经不复存在了。
entries.en: We received a distress signal from the headmaster of the Artisan Troupe. Their last station and cultural haven has been destroyed. There were few survivors, and the troupe is essentially no more.

entries.zh: 在摧毁艺术家联盟的空间站后，我们发现残骸中有大量可供回收的资源。舱室中储存的捐赠物、礼品与作品现在漂浮在太空之中，可供我们随意回收取用。
entries.en: After having destroyed the Artisan Troupe's station we found many resources to salvage from the wreckage. Donations, gifts and creations stacked in its halls now drift in space, ready for the taking.

entries.zh: 在摧毁了那个漂浮在[station_system.GetName]星系的空间站之后，我们在遗骸中发现了大量的珍贵资源。
entries.en: After destroying the station facility floating in the [station_system.GetName] system, we have found plenty of valuable resources amongst its remains.

entries.zh: 策展人
entries.en: Curators

entries.zh: 也许你正在疑惑我身后壁画上图案的意义。这是个好问题，答案也会十分有趣。只需要1.5亿亿能量币你便可以得到这个问题的解答。
entries.en: Perhaps you are wondering about the significance of the shapes you see on the mural behind me. That is a good question with a very interesting answer! The fee for this information is 15 quadrillion energy credits.

entries.zh: 我们是策展人，欢迎你们，请问你们需要什么服务？
entries.en: You have reached the Curators. How may we assist you?

entries.zh: 你们知不知道这次对话正在被七个来自不同领域的亚空间实体所密切地监听着？唉，想和他们交流是不可能的，因为你们的文明远不具备能与他们交流的通讯技术。
entries.en: Did you know that this conversation is being closely monitored by entities from seven different subspace realms? Alas, I fear that the technology to communicate with them is too far beyond the present capabilities of your civilization to do you any good.

entries.zh: 不用担心，我们已经更新了档案系统，[Root.GetName]的信息已经被记入了档案以供后辈们查阅。即使在你的帝国经历不可避免的消亡后，你们仍将在档案中被铭记。
entries.en: Fear not. We have updated our archives with information about the [Root.GetName] for future generations. You will be remembered long after the inevitable collapse of your star nation.

entries.zh: 我想告诉你的东西有很多，但我不能白白免费地告诉你。这个空间站需要很多能源来维持运转…我们必须考虑收支的平衡。
entries.en: There is so much I wish I could tell you, but I simply can't do it for free. This space station requires a lot of energy to operate... we must consider our overhead.

entries.zh: 谨代表策展人协会向您问候，请问您有什么需要的吗？
entries.en: Greetings on behalf of the Curator order. Was there something you wanted?

entries.zh: 我们一向很高兴能和你们的政府进行贸易，我们这里还有一些科技资源，你们有兴趣吗？
entries.en: As always, it is a pleasure doing business with your government. Can we interest you in some technology?

entries.zh: 很高兴见到你。我很肯定今天我们可以达成一些互利互惠的协定。
entries.en: It is good to see you. I am sure we can come to some sort of mutually beneficial agreement before this day is over.

entries.zh: 知识一旦落入了恶毒之徒的手中，就会变得相当危险。但我们能怎么办呢？毕竟我们需要能源才能运营下去……
entries.en: Knowledge in the wrong gripping appendages can be dangerous, but what can we do? We need energy to keep the lights on...

entries.zh: [Root.GetSpeciesName]，你们不知道的事情还有很多。求求你……让我们教授你们更多有关这个宇宙的知识吧。
entries.en: There is much that you do not yet know, [Root.GetSpeciesName]. Please... let us educate you about the universe.

entries.zh: 我们持有整个星系的详细星图，这是从上百种不同的物种处收集来的信息的汇总。也许这能提起你们的兴趣？
entries.en: We possess detailed star charts of the entire galaxy, gathered by explorers from a hundred different races. Perhaps they would be of interest to you?

entries.zh: 知识就是一切，它们必须被守护。
entries.en: Knowledge is everything. It must be preserved.

entries.zh: 与[curator_enclave_country.GetName]的第一次接触
entries.en: First Contact with the [curator_enclave_country.GetName]

entries.zh:
您好，星际旅行者，我们是策展人。

我们遵从的古训自万古之前便由星系中的支配力量所制定。我们献身于保存世间所有的知识，来避免星系再次陷入荒蛮与死寂的黑暗时期。

但我们失败了。

我们只留下了很少的幸存者，但相比我们的前辈，我们完成自己神圣使命的决心丝毫没有动摇。我们有意与你分享一些我们的知识……当然，这不是无偿的。
entries.en:
Greetings, star travelers. We are the Curators.

Our ancient order was established eons ago by the various galactic powers in ascendancy at the time. We were dedicated towards the preservation of all knowledge, in an effort to safeguard the galaxy from descending into yet another dark age of mass extinctions and barbarism.

We failed.

Few of us remain today, but we are no less committed to our sacred mission than our predecessors were. We are willing to share some of our knowledge with you... for a price.

entries.zh: 幸会，宇宙中的探险家。与你进行通话的是[curator_enclave_country.GetName]。也许你已经知晓我们古训中的信条。和其他城邦中的策展人同行们一样，只要你们能满足我们的要求，我们便愿意同你们交易。
entries.en: Well met, explorers. You are speaking to the [curator_enclave_country.GetName]. Perhaps you are already familiar with the tenets of our ancient order. Like our esteemed colleagues in the other Curator enclaves, we are willing to trade provided that you can meet our rates.

entries.zh: 很高兴见到你们。
entries.en: Well met.

entries.zh: 我们对你们绘制的§Y新星图§!很感兴趣。
entries.en: We are interested in procuring §Ynew star charts§!.

entries.zh: 你可以援助我们的§Y研究§!么？
entries.en: Can you aid us in our §Yresearch§!?

entries.zh: 策展人已经在增进我们的研究能力了。
entries.en: The Curators are already improving our research capabilities.

entries.zh: 告诉我们关于宇宙的§Y奥秘§!。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Ymysteries§! of the universe.

entries.zh: 我们能否招募你们的一名§Y科学家§!呢？
entries.en: Could we recruit one of your §Yscientists§!?

entries.zh: 我们已经招募了一名策展人科学家。
entries.en: We already employ a Curator scientist.

entries.zh: $requires_enclave_opinion$§G+50§!。
entries.en: $requires_enclave_opinion$ §G+50§!.

entries.zh: 你能分享一下那些知识的基本原理吗？
entries.en: Can you share the fundamental principles of knowledge?

entries.zh: 我们已经获得了策展人分享的知识原理。
entries.en: We have already shared the Curator principles.

entries.zh: $leviathans.500.d.opinion$
entries.en: $leviathans.500.d.opinion$

entries.zh: 能否告诉我们你们的§Y其他主顾§!的信息？
entries.en: Can you tell us about your §Yother customers§!?

entries.zh: 你对§Y$lgates$§!有何了解？
entries.en: What do you know about the §Y$lgates$§!?

entries.zh: [curator_enclave_country.GetName]要花上近十年才能发现新的§Y$clue$§!。
entries.en: It takes the [curator_enclave_country.GetName] approximately a decade to identify each new §Y$clue$§!.

entries.zh: 你可以帮助我们§Y生态园§!的繁育吗？
entries.en: Can you help us populate our §YVivarium§!?

entries.zh: $requires_enclave_opinion$§G+80§!。
entries.en: $requires_enclave_opinion$ §G+80§!.

entries.zh: 你可以对我们的§Y收藏§!提供支援吗？
entries.en: Can you assist us with our §YCollection§!?

entries.zh: 我们很抱歉，但我们目前没有什么可以提供的。试着去收集、展示更多的$specimens$吧。也许我们到时候就能分享更多专业知识了。
entries.en: We apologize, but we have nothing to offer you at this time. Try collecting and displaying more $specimens$. Perhaps we can then share our expertise.

entries.zh: 我们很抱歉，但我们已经没什么可以提供给你们了！你们的收藏真是蔚为壮观。很荣幸这个星系里能有你们这样的合作者。\n\n你们就是知识保护的无上财富。
entries.en: We apologize, but we have nothing left to offer you! Your collection is truly magnificent. We are honored to have you as a partner in our galaxy.\n\nYou are an asset to the preservation of knowledge.

entries.zh: 尊敬的顾客，我们教团感谢你。
entries.en: Our order thanks you, esteemed customer.

entries.zh: [root.GetSpeciesAdj]，感谢你。愿明晰与好奇心常伴汝身。
entries.en: Thank you, [root.GetSpeciesAdj]. Clarity and curiosity be with you.

entries.zh: 很高兴和你做生意！我们敏锐的见解和无价的记录能如何为你服务？
entries.en: A pleasure doing business with you. How else might our keen insights and inestimable records be of service to you?

entries.zh: 你们还有什么好东西？
entries.en: What else did you have to offer?

entries.zh: §Y太空城邦：§!策展人科研协助
entries.en: §YEnclave:§! The Curators Research Aid

entries.zh: 当然。我们准备将我们庞大的数据库对你们进行部分开放，为期十标准年。这应该会对你们行星§H研究实验室§!的科学研究起到巨大的推动作用。\n\n自不用说，我们要为这样的服务收取一定的报酬。不过我认为你一定会感觉我们的价格十分实惠。
entries.en: Of course. We are prepared to offer you limited access to our extensive databanks for a period of ten standard years. This should provide a significant boost to the research efforts of your planetside §HResearch Labs§!.\n\nWe will require compensation for this service, naturally, but I think you'll find that our prices are very reasonable.

entries.zh: 我们乐意购买这项服务。
entries.en: We would like to purchase this service.

entries.zh: 明智的选择，[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]的后人们会称赞你的选择的。
entries.en: A wise choice, that future generations of [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] will no doubt laud you for.

entries.zh: 未解之谜
entries.en: Mysteries

entries.zh: 在我们星系中的一些特定的恒星系里，潜藏着极其强大的存在。耗费了巨大的人力物力，策展人的调查人员煞费苦心地收集了他们的信息，有了这些信息，你在下次遇见它们时应该可以更容易地对付他们。
entries.en: There are exceedingly powerful entities lurking within certain star systems in our galaxy. At great cost in both lives and resources, Curator agents have painstakingly gathered knowledge that should make these beings easier to deal with the next time you encounter them.

entries.zh: 跟我们说些§Y新进展§!吧。
entries.en: Tell us about §Ysomething new§!.

entries.zh: 这个可能你会有兴趣……我们在你的§Y情报日志§!中标记了一个恒星系。
entries.en: This might interest you... We have marked a star system in your §YSituation Log§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Ether_Drake$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Ether_Drake$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Enigmatic_Fortress$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Enigmatic_Fortress$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Stellar_Devourer$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Stellar_Devourer$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Dimensional_Horror$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Dimensional_Horror$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Alien_Hive$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Alien_Hive$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Infinity_Machine$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Infinity_Machine$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Automated_Dreadnought$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Automated_Dreadnought$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Wraith$§!的事。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Wraith$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Voidspawn$§!。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Voidspawn$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Scavenger_Bot$§!。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Scavenger_Bot$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Elderly_Tiyanki$§!。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Elderly_Tiyanki$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Toxic_God$§!。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Toxic_God$§!.

entries.zh: 给我们讲讲§Y$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$§!。
entries.en: Tell us about the §Y$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$§!.

entries.zh: 我们的舰队面对它该如何作战？
entries.en: How would our current fleet fare against it in battle?

entries.zh: 你的舰队差劲，太差劲。\n\n等等，难不成你想要去……我的天哪，就用你的这丁点舰队？那，那会变成一边倒的屠杀。
entries.en: Poorly. Very poorly.\n\nWait a second, you're not actually thinking of...? My goodness, with the ships you have? It... it would be a slaughter!

entries.zh: 我强烈不建议你进行作战。你的攻击与其说是威胁它，更像是无谓的吵闹。
entries.en: I would strongly advise against it. Your attacks would likely be more of an annoyance than a threat.

entries.zh: 嗯……没错……没错，我想事实上你还是有很大的机会的。如果你联合你的整个舰队的话……我提醒你这场胜利不会轻松，但是起码你有胜利的可能性。
entries.en: Hmmm, yes... Yes, I suppose you might actually stand a chance. If you combined your entire fleet... It would not be an easy victory, mind you, but one that is at least within the realm of possibility.

entries.zh: 你的舰队是一支强大的舰队，甚至比得上一些被我们策展人编年史记载着的最伟大的无敌舰队。胜利掌握在你的手中。
entries.en: Yours is a mighty fleet, comparable to some of the greatest armadas recorded in the annals of the Curator Order. Victory is certainly within your reach.

entries.zh: 我们愿意建造一个§Y共享智库§!。
entries.en: We would like to establish a mutual §YThink Tank§!.

entries.zh: 智库
entries.en: Think Tank

entries.zh: 是的……是的，这样一个设施将会有益于全星系的科学发展。你可以在一个与我们共享星系的恒星基地里修建这个智库。我们的策展人将与你的科学家共处。
entries.en: Yes... yes, such a facility would benefit the advancement of Galactic Science. You may build this Think Tank at your starbase in the system you share with us. Our Curators will come to mingle with your scientists.

entries.zh: 棒极了。你们还有什么好东西？
entries.en: Excellent. What else do you have to offer?

entries.zh: 我们现在可以在§Y[curator_system.GetName]§!星系建造§H策展人智库§!这一恒星基地建筑了。
entries.en: We can now build the §HCurator Think Tank§! Starbase Building in the §Y[curator_system.GetName]§! system.

entries.zh: 我们现在可以在§Y[curator_system.GetName]§!星系建造§H策展人智库§!驿站模块了。
entries.en: We can now build the §HCurator Think Tank§! Waystation Module in the §Y[curator_system.GetName]§! system.

entries.zh: 虚空孳孽
entries.en: Voidspawn

entries.zh: 如果我们没猜错的话，虚空孳孽来自很远的地方。我们认为它是某种巨大无比的星系际捕食者的后代，他们会在虚空中寻找猎物。尽管我们从未遭遇过活的个体，我们听说过虚空孳孽的成年体所过之处，皆是破坏与混乱的故事。据说星球会在它们的阴影下溃烂。
entries.en: If our suspicions hold true, the Voidspawn is far away from home. We believe it is the progeny of an extragalactic predator of unthinkable proportions: one that stalks the void of space in search of its prey. Though we have never before encountered a live specimen, we have heard tales of the destruction and chaos grown Voidspawn leave in their wake. It is said that worlds fester under their shadow.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.a$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.a$

entries.zh:
据我们所知，母体会在恒星的轨道上产下星球大小的蛋，并花费数千年来孵化，有时甚至久到足以在蛋壳上发展出大气层与有机生命。

它们以活体物质为食，而成年虚空孳孽据说会对所有活物造成一种奇怪的影响。幸运的是，这只幼体似乎被其父母抛弃了。

或许我们最好该趁它尚未成熟之时将它消灭？
entries.en:
From what we can tell, the mother lays its planet-sized eggs in orbit of a star, where they then incubate for thousands of years, sometimes even long enough to develop an atmosphere and organic life.

They feed off of living matter, and adult Voidspawn are said to exert a strange influence on all living things. Fortunately this spawn seems to have been abandoned by its parents.

Perhaps it would be best to stifle the creature while it is still young and vulnerable?

entries.zh: 该怎么击败它？
entries.en: How is it defeated?

entries.zh: 我们从未听说有谁曾击败过成年虚空孳孽，但这只才刚刚出生。虚空孳孽会喷出腐蚀性的黏液和尖刺，连最厚的装甲都可以烧穿，但涂上一层抗酸涂层可以减缓这一过程。我们会为你们提供帮助。虚空孳孽对我们所有人都是个威胁。
entries.en: We have never heard of a grown Voidspawn being defeated in battle, but this one is newly hatched. The Voidspawn projects corrosive spittle and spikes that can burn through the thickest of armor, but applying a protective acid-proof coating may slow its progress. We will help you make it. The Voidspawn is a threat to us all.

entries.zh: 拾荒者
entries.en: Scavenger

entries.zh: 啊，废品机器人。拾荒者是一个失落时代的奇特造物。它无止尽地在残骸场中搜寻，将从无数残骸中搜获的枪炮，引擎，材料焊至自己的外壳上。其体量与火力数百年以来一直以这种方式提升，而且毫不减缓。\n\n如果有足够的时间与废品，没有人知道它到底能将自己造得多大。
entries.en: Ah, the scrap bot. The Scavenger is a curious construct from a lost age. Endlessly it searches through the debris fields of the galaxy, welding the guns, engines, and materials scavenged from countless derelicts onto its own hull. Its mass and firepower have been increasing in such a fashion for centuries, with no sign of relenting.\n\nNo-one knows if there is an upper limit to how massive it could become, given enough time and scrap to work with.

entries.zh: 当初是谁造了它？
entries.en: Who built it, initially?

entries.zh: 不幸的是，关于拾荒者的起源并没有准确的数据。有些科学家认为它是一个失落帝国的废品回收机器人，但出了故障，其原本用途早已被硬件劣化埋没了。也有人认为它原本是一个微小的纳米机器人，在其程序驱动下，利用其周围环境来不断地使自己变大变强。还有人认为它当初是机器人舰长，是数千年前一场星际大战的唯一幸存者。因其文明突然且彻底的毁灭，导致其逻辑系统无法挽回地受损了。\n\n当然，这些都只是猜测。
entries.en: Unfortunately, no definitive data regarding the Scavenger's origin is known to exist. Some researchers believe it to be a malfunctioning scrap collection service machine from a lost empire, its purpose long since muddled by hardware degradation. Others believe it to have originated as a single microscopic nanobot, programmed to endlessly build itself larger and stronger by exploiting its environment. Still others reckon it may have started out as a robotic ship's captain; the sole survivor of an intergalactic battle waged millennia ago. Perhaps its reasoning systems were irrevocably damaged by the sudden destruction of its entire civilization.\n\nOf course, this is all just speculation.

entries.zh: 我们可以与它沟通吗？
entries.en: Can we communicate with it?

entries.zh: 多年来许多人都试图与拾荒机器人沟通，或者转而尝试更改其程序。不幸的是，这些远征队大多数都变成了拾荒者机器人身处的宇宙垃圾场的一部分。只有那些跑得比它还快的才活了下来。\n\n它身上焊接的重炮火力已经足以单枪匹马消灭整个帝国的舰队——而且这样的情况可能已经发生过不止一次了。当然，这种毁灭性的遭遇只会进一步增强拾荒者，为其提供更多可利用的舰船部件。
entries.en: Over the years there have been many attempts to communicate with it, or else to alter the programming of the Scavenger. Unfortunately, most of those expeditions ended up part of the cosmic scrap yards where the Scavenger Bot dwells. Only those who were able to outrun it survived.\n\nThe Scavenger has welded enough heavy artillery onto its patchwork frame to single-handedly destroy an entire nation's fleet - an event that may already have occurred on more than one occasion. Of course, any such destructive encounters would only have served to further strengthen the Scavenger, providing it with more ship components to repurpose.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.b$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.b$

entries.zh: 你可能已经推测到了：拾荒者并非按照任何明确的现成图纸而造。因此，它的某些部件并不太……合身，导致了一些不连续的结构弱点。当然，外行人一眼看不出这些弱点，但我们的先进传感器已经设法确定了它们的位置。\n\n让你的舰队集中火力攻击我们在拾荒者上标明的这些部位，应该可以大幅降低击溃它所需要倾斜的火力。
entries.en: As you may have surmised: the Scavenger was not built according to any definitive, pre-existing schematics. As a result, some of its parts fit together... less than optimally, leading to a discrete number of structural weaknesses. Of course, to the uninitiated, most of these are obscured from view - but our advanced sensors have managed to isolate them.\n\nTell your fleets to focus fire on the indicated sections of the Scavenger's hull, and it should substantially reduce the amount of damage the construct is able to take before collapsing.

entries.zh: 再给我们讲讲它的起源。
entries.en: Remind us about its origins.

entries.zh: 再给我们讲讲与它沟通的尝试。
entries.en: Remind us about attempts at communicating with it.

entries.zh: 缇扬奇族母
entries.en: Tiyanki Matriarch

entries.zh: 真壮观，不是吗？一只消瘦的老族母，她的外皮在漫漫岁月中变白变硬，战列舰在她的触手中就像牡蛎壳一般脆弱。几十年前，我们的科学家听说有一位舰长，发誓要狩猎族母至星系尽头。不过，考虑到族母仍然存活，我们可以肯定他未能成功。
entries.en: Magnificent, is she not? A wizened old Matriarch, her hide bleached and hardened by the eons, her tentacles capable of snapping the hulls of battleships like oyster shells. Decades ago, our researchers heard rumors of a captain sworn to hunt the Matriarch to the ends of the galaxy. However, considering her continued existence, we cannot imagine he met with success.

entries.zh: 为什么族母比其它缇扬奇要大许多？
entries.en: Why is the Matriarch so much larger than other Tiyanki?

entries.zh: 她惊人的巨大身躯实属异常。我们认为族母是来自另一星系的漂流者，那里的缇扬奇与我们星系中的缇扬奇进化产生了分歧，变得更大更强。\n\n当然，另一种可能性是族母只是得了一种巨大畸形症——不过这无法解释她的长寿。
entries.en: Her incredible size is an anomaly, to be sure. We believe the Matriarch is a wanderer from another galaxy in deep space, where a species of Tiyanki far greater in size and strength diverged evolutionarily from the Tiyanki found in our own.\n\nOf course, it is also possible the Matriarch is simply suffering from an advanced form of gigantism - though this would fail to explain her extended lifespan.

entries.zh: 你对那位狩猎族母的舰长有何了解？
entries.en: What do you know about the captain hunting the Matriarch?

entries.zh: 很少。那位舰长很可能从另一个星系追着族母来到了这里。不过，为何有人会蠢到挑战可以单枪匹马消灭整支舰队的生物仍是个谜。
entries.en: Very little. It is quite possible the captain chased the Matriarch here from another galaxy. Though why one would be foolish enough to challenge a creature capable of destroying entire fleets with just one vessel is beyond us.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.b$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.b$

entries.zh:
族母非常强大，但并非坚不可摧。尽管她的装甲外壳可以抵御多种投射物，她仍有一个可观的弱点。

在她的背上插着一枚巨型质子鱼雷，这是最近一场战斗中留下的仍未愈合的伤口。尽管那颗鱼雷似乎故障了，我们的扫描显示它仍可以引爆，只要用一道特定的能源脉冲诱发即可。

我们现在将详情发送给你。
entries.en:
The Matriarch is formidable, but not indestructible. While her armored hide protects her from a wide range of projectiles, she carries with her a remarkable weakness.

There is a massive proton torpedo lodged in her back: a wound from a recent battle that has healed poorly. While seemingly defective, our scans of the torpedo suggest it can still be detonated, if agitated with a specific energy pulse.

We will transmit the details to you now.

entries.zh: 再给我们讲讲为何族母比其它缇扬奇要大许多。
entries.en: Remind us why the Matriarch is larger than other Tiyanki.

entries.zh: 再给我们讲讲那位狩猎族母的舰长。
entries.en: Remind us about the captain hunting the Matriarch.

entries.zh: 毒圣
entries.en: The Toxic God

entries.zh: 毒性神祗是一个捉摸不透的存在。几千年来它在星系内来回游荡，偶尔会选择某个星球喷洒毒液——我们只能猜测这是其生命循环的某个自然阶段。我们听说上次它被目击到是在§Y[toxic_god_system.GetName]§!星系。
entries.en: The Toxic Entity is an elusive being. It has roamed the galaxy for millennia, occasionally choosing to spurt venom at worlds in what we can only imagine is a natural stage of its life cycle. We have heard that it has been tracked to the §Y[toxic_god_system.GetName]§! system.

entries.zh: 毒性神祗是一个捉摸不透的存在。几千年来它在星系内来回游荡，偶尔会选择某个星球喷洒毒液——我们只能猜测这是其生命循环的某个自然阶段。当然，你肯定早就知道了！\n\n我们很抱歉，但是我们没法帮你找到它现在所在的位置——我们的全体线人都有好一阵子没看到它了。
entries.en: The Toxic Entity is an elusive being. It has roamed the galaxy for millennia, occasionally choosing to spurt venom at worlds in what we can only imagine is a natural stage of its life cycle. But you already knew this, of course!\n\nWe are sorry, but we cannot help you find its present whereabouts - it has not been spotted by any of our contacts for quite some time.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.a$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.a$

entries.zh: 重新给我们讲讲你对它有什么了解。
entries.en: Remind us what you know of it.

entries.zh: 没有文献记载毒性神祗究竟从何而来。第一次目击是在数千年之前，自那以后每过几个世纪就有人目击过。某些人视其为神明，但具体如何得由你自己判断。我们能够告诉你的是，它是一个极度令人畏惧的有机生物，有着节肢动物的特征。有报告表明，它的体型相当巨大，上面甚至发展出了一整个生态系统。当然，获取其生物学样本的难度可以预想是有多么困难了。
entries.en: It is not documented where the Toxic Entity came from. The first sighting was several thousand years ago, and since then it has been seen every few centuries. Some have called it a deity, but that is for you to decide. What we can tell you is that it is an extremely formidable organic being with arthropoid characteristics. Reports suggest that it is sufficiently large that an entire ecosystem has developed on it, though acquiring samples of its biology has proved understandably challenging.

entries.zh: 该怎么击败它？
entries.en: How is it defeated?

entries.zh: 重新给我们讲讲应该如何同它战斗。
entries.en: Remind us how we can fight it.

entries.zh: 过去撞见它的人中有少数几个幸存者。根据报告，它带有腐蚀性的毒液能够烧蚀任何形态的装甲。护盾相对来说更加有用一丁点。此外，在它的背上生活的那些生物在剧毒实体受到威胁的时候，会像蜂群一样发动攻击。我们只能建议你带着压倒性的军力去接近它。
entries.en: There have been few survivors to its past encounters. According to reports, its corrosive poisons are able to burn through all forms of armor. Shields are only slightly more useful. Furthermore, the creatures living on its back will supposedly act as an attack swarm when it is threatened. We can only suggest you approach it with overwhelming force.

entries.zh: $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$
entries.en: $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$

entries.zh: 那个颇为神经质的自动化机械体来到这个星系的时间并不长，但不要被这种新奇所迷惑。$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$的创造者们在被一台专横的机器同化之前，就已经是他们所在领域中最杰出的工程师之一。我们不知道自那时起，那个机器意识遭遇了怎样严酷的命运，但从哨兵那痛苦的扭动来看：情况似乎相当不稳定。如果你决定满足自己的好奇心，务必小心行事。
entries.en: That rather twitchy automaton is a relative newcomer to the galaxy, but don't be fooled by such novelty. The $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$'s creators were counted among the finest engineers in their sector even before they were assimilated by a tyrannical machine. We do not know what harsh fate has befallen the machine consciousness since then, but if the Sentinel's agonized writhing is anything to go by: the whole situation appears quite volatile. Tread carefully, should you decide to slake your curiosity.

entries.zh: 恕我冒昧，但我以为您会比我们更了解此事！与我们所研究的对象相比，那个颇为不安的自动化机械体是个新面孔，但作为对手同样令人畏惧。\n\n我们知道，即便在被同化之前，$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$背后的工程师们也被认为是该领域最优秀的人才。因此，那艘战舰不容小觑。我们不太清楚的是，这艘船是如何与[origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]如此疏远的。从“哨兵”痛苦的扭动来看，我们推测情况仍然相当不稳定。您是否同意这一评估，[root.GetSpeciesName]？
entries.en: Forgive my impertinence, but I assumed you would know more about it than we do! That rather twitchy automaton is a newcomer compared to what we usually study here, but is no less fearsome an opponent.\n\nWe know that even before they were assimilated, the engineers behind the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ were counted among the finest in their sector. That warship is therefore not to be underestimated. What is less clear to us is how the vessel became so detached from the [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]. We gather from the Sentinel's agonized writhing that the whole situation remains quite volatile. Would you agree with assessment, [root.GetSpeciesName]?

entries.zh: 你是说它在守护着什么吗？
entries.en: You say it is guarding something?

entries.zh: 正是，尽管我们并不确切知道是什么。我们的一些联系人认为，哨兵正在保卫分裂的[origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]所剩下的任何东西；另一些人则暗示，这颗星球本身蕴藏着某种宝藏。我们所知道的是，这艘战舰的建造比其[origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetAdj]同类坚固得多，甚至高出一个数量级。无论它在保护什么，$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$都在坚持，尽管有明显的痛苦迹象，甚至可能是极度的煎熬。
entries.en: Indeed, though we do not know precisely what. Some of our contacts believe the Sentinel is defending whatever remains of the splintered [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]; others suggest the planet itself holds some treasure. What we do know is that this warship was built more robustly than any of its [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetAdj] peers by an order of magnitude. Whatever it is protecting out there, the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ perseveres despite clear signs of distress, or perhaps even agony.

entries.zh: 我们宁愿不谈这件事。
entries.en: We prefer not to talk about it.

entries.zh: 完全可以理解。我们只是出于好奇。\n\n还有其他我可以帮您的吗？
entries.en: Quite understandable. We are merely curious.\n\nIs there anything else I can help you with?

entries.zh: 我们能在哪里找到这个实体？
entries.en: Where can we find this entity?

entries.zh: 鉴于您是我们较为信任的客户之一……我可以告知您，$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$最后一次被目击到是在守护§Y[origin_unplugged_machine_legacy_core.GetName]星系§!\n\n考虑到我们对这艘饱经战火、问题重重的战舰仍然知之甚少，请您放心：我们将以极大的兴趣观察您与它的遭遇细节！
entries.en: Seeing as how you are one of our more trustworthy clients... I can tell you the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ was last seen guarding the §Y[origin_unplugged_machine_legacy_core.GetName] system§!.\n\nGiven how much we still do not know about this ferociously troubled warship, rest assured: we shall observe the particulars of your encounter with keen interest!

entries.zh: 我们从策展人那里购买了这些坐标，他们报告称$NAME_Opus_Sentinel$最后一次出现在该区域。
entries.en: We bought these coordinates from the Curators, who report the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ was last seen in this area.

entries.zh: 雇佣科学官
entries.en: Hire Scientist

entries.zh: 我们愿意提供我们之中最杰出的科学家来换取你们的资助。你们要知道这种提议可不是谁都能轻易获得的。\n\n当然，在做出人员安排之前，你必须准备好合适数量的……资金赞助。
entries.en: We are willing to pledge the services of one of our most brilliant scientists to your cause. This is not an offer we make to just anyone, you understand!\n\nA suitable... donation will of course be necessary, before traveling arrangements can be made.

entries.zh: 当然，我们会给你们资助的。
entries.en: Of course. You shall have your donation.

entries.zh: 很好，你们现在可以随意的使用我们这个时代最杰出的头脑了！
entries.en: Excellent. You will now have unfettered access to one of the greatest minds of our time!

entries.zh: 我们每次只能雇佣§Y一名§!§H策展人科学家§!。
entries.en: We may only employ §Yone§! §HCurator scientist§! at a time.

entries.zh: 共享原理
entries.en: Shared Principles

entries.zh: 我们愿意向你们的集体灌输知识的基本原理。这个流程非常严格，而且只有在共同意识的情况下才能进行。\n\n即使对我们来说，这也不是一件容易的事情。成本并非微不足道。但在所有商品中，知识仍是最宝贵的。
entries.en: We are willing to infuse your collective with the fundamental principles of knowledge. A serious procedure, and one only available to a shared consciousness.\n\nEven for us, it is no easy thing to achieve. The cost is not insignificant. But of all commodities, knowledge remains the most precious.

entries.zh: $leviathans.590.a$
entries.en: $leviathans.590.a$

entries.zh: 这是一笔划算的投资。
entries.en: A sound investment.

entries.zh: 策展人的基本原理已经分享给我们了。
entries.en: The fundamental principles of the Curators have already been shared with us.

entries.zh: 购买情报
entries.en: Buy Intelligence

entries.zh: 你们属于高信用的顾客，所以我们可以向你们透露某些我们的……低优先级顾客的消息。当然，该如何使用这些消息完全取决于你们自己。\n\n你想要了解什么？
entries.en: Since you are one of our trusted customers, we are able to divulge to you certain information on our... less favored clients. What you do with this information is entirely up to you, of course.\n\nWho do you want to know about?

entries.zh: 告诉我们[curator_customer_1.GetName]的情报吧。
entries.en: Tell us about the [curator_customer_1.GetName].

entries.zh: [curator_customer_2.GetName]的情报你们都知道些什么？
entries.en: What do you know of the [curator_customer_2.GetName]?

entries.zh: 我们希望了解关于[curator_customer_3.GetName]的情报。
entries.en: We wish to know about the [curator_customer_3.GetName].

entries.zh: 我们对[curator_customer_4.GetName]的情报感兴趣。
entries.en: The [curator_customer_4.GetName] is of interest to us.

entries.zh: 很好。情报很快就会通过星系最严密的星际数据链传输给你们。
entries.en: Excellent. The information will be transferred to you immediately via the most secure interstellar datalink in the galaxy.

entries.zh: $clues$
entries.en: $clues$

entries.zh:
$lgates$？是的，正如其它传送门一样，它们的历史比最古老的$gov_stagnant_ascendancy$还要久，但你们肯定已经知道这一点了。

它们为何不同？它们通往哪里？我们决定不要对这些谜团太过深究——“一朝被蛇咬，零点一七年怕井绳”这道理你懂的——但我们愿意分享一些可能与其有关的近期发现。

当然，不是免费的。
entries.en:
The $lgates$? Yes, like the other Gateways they predate even the oldest $gov_stagnant_ascendancy$, but we are sure you have figured that out already.

Why are they different? Where do they lead? We have opted not to delve too deeply into those particular mysteries - "thrice bitten, zero-point-seventeen shy" you know how it is - but we are willing to share some recent revelations that just might be related.

For a price.

entries.zh: 请说吧。
entries.en: Please do.

entries.zh: 看来我们真是高估你们了，你们的人根本不具备文明处事的能力。真是奇怪……我们通常在刚见面的时候就可以准确识别出某个物种是否具备好斗倾向。为什么对你们看走眼了呢。\n\n我们已经剥夺了你们对我们数据库的访问权限。
entries.en: It would appear that we grossly overestimated your capacity to act as a civilized nation. Strange... We are usually able to identify the violent ones at an early stage.\n\nWe have severed your access to our databanks, of course.

entries.zh: 你们这群笨蛋！袭击我们就等于放弃了知识，你们的后辈们将活在低科技水平的蛮荒之中！
entries.en: You fool! By attacking us, you are condemning future generations to lives of low-tech misery!

entries.zh: 你们受本能驱使而袭击我们，而现在你们要为此付出代价。我们将永远不再与[Root.GetName]分享我们的知识。
entries.en: Your base instincts compelled you to attack us, and now you must pay the price. We will never share our knowledge with the [Root.GetName] again.

entries.zh: [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]，我们慷慨相助，你们却不识好人心。一群野蛮的渣滓！
entries.en: We had so much to offer you [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural], and yet you would throw it all away. Neo-barbarian scum!

entries.zh: 你们已经成为整个策展人组织的敌人。
entries.en: You have been declared an enemy of the entire Curator Order.

entries.zh: 以太巨龙
entries.en: Ether Drake

entries.zh: 以太龙族这个物种并不适合在我们的宇宙中生存，最后的这只龙虽然很强，但也不是无敌的。
entries.en: The Ether Drake species is ill-suited to life in our universe. The last dragon is strong, but not invincible.

entries.zh: 这东西到底是什么玩意？
entries.en: What is it, really?

entries.zh:
传说中，以太巨龙的出现先于任何一个宇宙文明。它们曾经数量众多，但随着时代更迭他们的族群也在逐渐衰落。

可以说，此时此地并不适合它们的生存。它们似乎不大适应宇宙的物理法则，就好像它们是从其他的现实中进化而来一般。而这，正是事实所在。我们认为它们是来自一个我们宇宙开始之前就已终结的宇宙，也就是某次"大坍缩"中唯一的生还者。

离这里不远的那条龙恐怕是这个星系，乃至这个宇宙中最后的以太巨龙了。
entries.en:
By all accounts, the Ether Drakes predate all galactic civilization. There once were multitudes, but their race has been wasting away for eons.

They are ill-suited to life, here and now. Something about the physical laws of the universe does not agree with them, like they evolved in another reality. They did, in fact. We believe that they are but the last dregs of a universe that ended before ours began, the sole survivors of some "big crunch."

The dragon not far from here is the last of its kind in the galaxy, perhaps the universe.

entries.zh: 告诉我们如何才能击败它。
entries.en: Tell us how to defeat it.

entries.zh: 龙身上的鳞片对敲击节律有反应，更精确地说，特定的频率对它的皮下组织有着放松的作用，而那里控制着它们的用以移动与防护冲击的鳞片。这个条件反射曾是以太巨龙之间社交行为的关键环节，现在则成为了它的死穴。\n\n调整舰船火力平台的攻击节奏到一个特定的频率，可以有效地增加以太巨龙所受到的伤害。它并不是主动想生存在这个世界之中——一劳永逸地结束它的痛苦吧。
entries.en: Its scales respond to percussive rhythms. To be more precise, certain frequencies have a relaxing effect on the sub-dermal musculature controlling the positioning and shock absorption of their scale plates. A reflex that once played a key role in Ether Drake social interactions, it is now a clear and obvious weakness.\n\nAdjusting the firing pattern of your vessels according to a particular rhythm will greatly increase the damage you can inflict on the last dragon. It was never meant for our age - put it out of its misery.

entries.zh: 神秘堡垒
entries.en: Enigmatic Fortress

entries.zh: 这是一种已经没人会再建造的，异想天开，体型巨大且能自我维持的建筑。也许不建是明智的选择。
entries.en: It is the kind of absurd, massive and self-perpetuating construction that you don't see built anymore. Maybe that is for the best.

entries.zh: 任何造物都能被毁坏。
entries.en: Any structure can be destroyed.

entries.zh: 这座堡垒曾经被击毁过，但它总能恢复原状。一些古老的帝国曾经因未能揭开它更深层次的秘密，抑或是未能永久地毁灭它而陷入癫狂。这座堡垒对于维持自身是如此尽心尽力，令人不得不怀疑它是否还有其他的正经用途。
entries.en: The Fortress has been defeated before, but it always recovers. Some of the ancient empires of this galaxy were driven to madness by their vain efforts to unlock its deeper secrets, or else to permanently destroy it. It appears so focused on maintaining itself that we doubt it has any other serious purpose.

entries.zh: 堡垒可以进入吗？
entries.en: Can the fortress be entered?

entries.zh: 可以，而且已经有人进入过了，尽管那项尝试的壮举已经在时间的流逝中几乎被忘却。这座堡垒在关闭状态时仅能维持部分供能，不过它会尝试从附近摄取能量以迅速重启系统。请务必小心。
entries.en: It can and it has been, although that attempt is now nearly forgotten. The fortress maintains only partial power while in shutdown, however it will attempt to draw power from nearby sources in order to jump-start its systems again. Proceed with caution.

entries.zh: 是谁建造了这个堡垒？
entries.en: Who built the fortress?

entries.zh: 不管是谁，他们一定对于谜题与解密十分着迷。人们过去只从堡垒里面回收了一些形状奇怪的金属物件：这些古怪装置的零件，似乎设计上可以通过重新排列组成更加自然的形态。当时的回收人员并未能解开谜题，但所幸从堡垒中死里逃生。绝大多数人就没能活着出来了。
entries.en: Whoever they were, they must have been fond of puzzles and enigmas. The only items to have been recovered from the fortress are strange metal shapes: components of perplexing contraptions which seem designed to be rearranged into more satisfying forms. Those who brought them back did so because they failed, and they barely escaped with their lives. Many others didn't.

entries.zh: 它是如何驱动自己的？
entries.en: How is the fortress powered?

entries.zh: 动力系统一定是在建造最初舱体与安装防御系统之间的某个时候建造而成的。我们尚不清楚它的恢复方式，但我们发现堡垒中保存着巨量的暗物质。了解那些物质与以及其与黑洞的关系，是弄清堡垒长久以来运作方式的关键。\n\n没人曾经成功找到它的动力源，但这动力的来源似乎十分不稳定。
entries.en: The power system must have been built at a time between initial construction of the hull, and installation of its defense systems. The system's recovery method is unknown to us, but we have discovered that the fortress contains large quantities of dark matter. That substance and its relationship to black holes are key to understanding how the fortress has lasted so long.\n\nNo one has ever found the source of its power, but it is likely to be extremely volatile.

entries.zh: 重新给我们讲讲如何进入该建筑。
entries.en: Remind us about entering it.

entries.zh: 重新给我们讲讲该建筑的建造者。
entries.en: Remind us who built it.

entries.zh: 重新给我们讲讲该建筑的供能方式。
entries.en: Remind us how it is powered.

entries.zh: 噬星者
entries.en: Stellar Devourer

entries.zh: 就像你的帝国一样，噬星者是星系狩猎场中的一种新的寄生虫。它们从恐惧和核聚变中诞生，平时在星际间游荡。它们会潜进恒星内部，从内部汲取养分。另外，它们也很不想被打扰。
entries.en: The Stellar Devourer is a new parasite on the galactic hunting ground, not unlike your empire in many ways. It was born out of fear and nuclear fusion. It roams the galaxy, submerging itself into stars, feasting on them from within. And it certainly does not like being disturbed.

entries.zh:
这种恒星吞噬者是一种很罕见的生物，我们并不知道这种怪物的来源。我们手上现有的情报非常有限，只有极少数的情报提供源获得了与它们接触的第一手资料。

但是我们现有的资料都指向了一个事实：这是一种极其可怕的生物，它只会带来毁灭。

噬星者能够以聚变为食。我们得出了一个§Y非常§!有说服力的推断：它是暗物质和恒星物质在外部维度层面上融合的产物。它们潜进恒星内部，吞噬其中的物质来为其内部聚变反应堆提供燃料。它所到的恒星系，无一逃得过灭亡的命运。在它的盛宴之后，行星们要么像冰一样粉碎，要么暴露在它胃中的第二太阳之下被烧尽。

它贪得无厌，永远不会停下吞噬的脚步。当你注视着它的时候，你会从中看到为了生存而透露出的无以言表的狂怒。
entries.en:
The star-feaster is a rare breed. A new type of beast of unknown origin. The accounts we have collected are few and sparse with intel. Few sources even have firsthand experience with the thing.

All our data points to the same fact, however: it is a terror that brings nothing but ruin.

The Stellar Devourer is capable of feeding off of fusion itself. Our §Yvery§! educated guess is that its biology is the result of some outer-dimensional fusing of dark matter and solar matter. It dives into stars, feasting on their innards in order to fuel its own, internal fusion reactor. It brings death to all systems it reaches. Either they shatter like ice after its banquet, or they burn from being exposed to a second sun from within the being's belly.

It wants to feed, and it will stop at nothing to get its share. When you gaze at it, what you see is a survivor's raw fury.

entries.zh: 我们目前唯一确定的事实是，噬星者最重要的部分是它的集成核心。它极度需要维持其内部的反应炉运转，避免让寒冷的虚空接触到它内部使其自行崩塌。没有那些恒星物质，它就没办法存活。\n\n这是一个你们可以利用的缺陷。你们可以将武器按照我们提供的标准来进行校准，这样你们就能穿破保护其消化系统的外层组织。打伤它，你就能看到它的内部物质喷射出来，扩散到整个星系。
entries.en: The only thing we know for sure is that the collected core is the most important aspect of the Stellar Devourer. The creature desperately needs to keep its furnace burning, lest the cold void of space reaches its vital organs deeper within and makes it collapse in on itself. Without that stellar matter, it is nothing.\n\nYou can use this to your advantage. Calibrate your weapons to our specifications and you can then home in on the very membranes that hold the Devourer's digestive system together. Wound it and you will see its innards gush out across the solar system.

entries.zh: 位面之魇
entries.en: Dimensional Horror

entries.zh: 我们的设备发现有一物体冲入我们的世界，同时还检测到了巨大的能量涌动。
entries.en: Our instruments monitored the immense energy surge when this entity pierced its way into our realm of existence.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.a$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.a$

entries.zh: 这种完全是由怨恨组成的生物，诞生于另外一个位面。那里非常像是许多太空文明所信仰的宗教里描述的地狱。目前我们看到的还只是它的冰山一角——这只怪物的全貌应该比现在的样子还大上几倍。\n\n所幸，它没能完全转移至我们的宇宙。如若不然，它可能早已经将所有的生命赶尽杀绝了。
entries.en: It is a creature of pure malice, born in a dimension that bears more than a striking resemblance to the realm of Hell as described by many galactic religions. What we are seeing is but a small part of a greater whole - the creature in its entirety is multitudes larger.\n\nIt is very fortunate that it was unable to complete its transition into our universe. Had it been successful, the creature would likely have consumed all life in the galaxy by now.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.b$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.b$

entries.zh: 位面之魇最大的弱点是它通往我们宇宙的位面传送门——没有传送门，它就不能在我们的宇宙中存活下去。我们已经确认了传送门能量矩阵中几个薄弱的位置，用传统的武器就能对其造成伤害。现在开始传送目标坐标点。
entries.en: The dimensional portal that it spawned from is its greatest weakness - without it, it cannot exist in our universe. We have identified several weak points in the portal's energy matrix that could be exploited by conventional weapons. Transmitting targeting coordinates now.

entries.zh: 小行星蜂群
entries.en: Asteroid Hiver

entries.zh: 这些令人感到烦躁的虫子曾经比现在更多，它们的足迹遍布整个星系。那个时候，当你航行通过任意一个小行星带时，你都会发现有小虫子围绕着你的船只。
entries.en: These annoying pests were once far more prevalent in our galaxy. There was a time when you couldn't cruise through a random asteroid belt without the little beasts swarming around your ship!

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.a$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.a$

entries.zh: 它们是一种具有侵略性的硅基生物。尽管它们一度对太空文明构成巨大威胁，但过去的50万年来，它们遭到大量的捕杀，剩下的都隐遁了起来。\n\n尽管流传着许多谣言，目前没有任何证据表明它们具备任何智慧生物的特征。它们喜欢在小行星里筑巢，并且攻击所有它们认为是有威胁的东西。
entries.en: They are an aggressively territorial silicon-based life form. Although they once posed a significant threat to spacefaring civilizations, their numbers have been severely culled over the last 500,000 years and the surviving members of their species are fairly reclusive.\n\nDespite rumors to the contrary, there is no evidence that they possess anything that could be described as sapient intelligence. They tend to nest inside asteroids, and they will attack anything which is perceived as a threat.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.b$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.b$

entries.zh: 这种生物喜欢用一种未知的物质包裹在他们的蜂巢小行星外面来防御舰载武器的攻击。但是这种物质并不能完全地覆盖在小行星的表面上。\n\n有了这些现在正传输给你的瞄准数据，你的飞船可以集中火力攻击未覆盖装甲的区域，大大提升攻击效果。
entries.en: The creatures have a tendency to coat their asteroid nests with some kind of unknown substance that acts as a potent armor against ship-based weapons. This substance is not perfectly applied across the entire surface of the asteroid, however.\n\nWith the targeting data we are transmitting to you now, your ships will be able to focus their fire on unprotected surface areas, greatly increasing the damage they inflict.

entries.zh: 无限神机
entries.en: Infinity Machine

entries.zh: 嗯对，这种色彩斑斓的机器出现于远古时代。我们对它的研究可以追溯到我们城邦建立之初。在我们之前已经有许多文明也对它进行了研究。\n\n这种机器已经不只是上古时代的产物了。根据我们现有的资料显示，它一直都存在着。但是，它所做的唯一的事情就是绕着黑洞转。我们对无限神机很感兴趣，但是我们明白这种东西对于你们来说还是太难理解了。
entries.en: Ah yes, the chromatic being from long ago. We have studied it for as long as our order has existed. As have several civilizations before us.\n\nThis machine is beyond ancient. For all we know, it has always been. And yet, all it does is orbit that black hole. It's fascinating to us, but we understand if it is too much for you to grasp.

entries.zh: 你口中笼统称为无限神机的存在，是无法进行回收的，更无法获得它的任何信息。整个星系中没有任何一个骇客或者工程师能透过它闪亮的外壳看到里面的任何东西——我们很清楚它里面藏着许多有价值的信息。我们也束手无策。我们既不知道它的用途，也不知道它接下去的任务是什么。
entries.en: The Infinity Machine, as you so bluntly call it, is impervious to extraction. No information comes out from it. No hacker or engineer in the entire galaxy has been able to see through its shiny exterior to gain a glimpse of the knowledge it so obviously withholds from us. We are at a loss. We neither know what it is for, nor what it aims to do once it's done.

entries.zh: 有一种办法大概可以摧毁它。我们虽然无法从它身上获得任何信息，但它的外壳还是可以破坏的。采矿者曾经无数次尝试过从它上面获取资源，但回来时全都狼狈不堪。不过他们发现了一些有趣的情况：无限神机并不像看起来那样坚不可摧。\n\n它是由一种能够调节其自身属性的材料构成。密度、弹性、温度，只有你想不到，没有它变不了的！它能够实时分析伤害，并及时改变外壳特性进行补偿。这样一来，外界的伤害就很难摧毁它了。你要做的，就是改变攻击的频率，调整导弹的热力输出，不管用什么攻击方式，想方设法地进行变化。这样你们才能克服无限神机外壳的适应性。
entries.en: There is perhaps one thing you could do to destroy it. We have been unable to retrieve information from it, but its hull is breakable. Miners have tried to gather resources from it at numerous times, only to come back with their ships barely holding together. But they did find something interesting: The Infinity Machine is not as rigid as it seems.\n\nIt is made of a material capable of changing its characteristics. Density, flexibility, heat, you name it! It can analyze damage in real time and change its shell to compensate, thus making itself harder to take down. Change your frequencies, adjust the thermal output of your missiles, whatever you people lumber around with, and keep changing them. That way you can get past its adaptive capabilities.

entries.zh: 自动无畏战舰
entries.en: Automated Dreadnought

entries.zh: 这是一个悲伤的故事。自动无畏战舰的主人已经过世百万年之久了，但是这些巨大的舰船还继续在它们帝国的废墟周围警戒着。
entries.en: A sad story. Its masters have been dead for millions of years, but this massive warship continues to stand vigil over the broken rubble of their empire.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.a$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.a$

entries.zh: 七百万年前，曾经有个伟大的星际帝国在我们的星系中一个不起眼的地方兴盛强大，这是那曾经无比强大的帝国的旗舰之一。历史往往都是相似的，这个帝国在一系列与邻国的惨烈战争中骤然消亡。\n\n你遇到的无畏战舰是他们最后的遗物。尽管船员们都已经去世，电脑系统还在尽职地巡逻。在这段漫长的时光中，无数人都曾想让这艘战舰安息——但没有一次成功。
entries.en: It was one of several flagships belonging to an unusually powerful interstellar empire that flourished in a small region of our galaxy some seven million years ago. As is so often the case, that empire was brought to a sudden and violent end at the hands of its neighbors in a series of very destructive wars.\n\nThe dreadnought you have encountered is the last of its kind, and it continues to dutifully patrol its assigned system despite the death of its crew. Many attempts have been made throughout the ages to put the old warship to its final rest - none successful.

entries.zh: $leviathans.510.b$
entries.en: $leviathans.510.b$

entries.zh: 设计之初，这艘无畏战舰应该载着大量的船员进行操作，但是现在它仅依靠着自动化系统来工作。这使得它在其中央计算机的中继节点受到干扰时将变得非常脆弱。
entries.en: The dreadnought was designed to operate with a large crew, but it now relies exclusively on automated systems to function. This makes the ship especially vulnerable to attacks that disrupt the relay nodes used by its central computer.

entries.zh: 幽魂
entries.en: Wraith

entries.zh: 神出鬼没的幽魂是一种令人烦躁的生物，如果它们能被称为生物的话。我们把它们当做是一种罕见但是极具破坏力的自然灾害。
entries.en: Spectral Wraiths are disturbing creatures, if they are creatures at all. We consider them a rare and extraordinarily efficient natural disaster.

entries.zh: 你对这种灾害有什么了解？
entries.en: What do you know about these disasters?

entries.zh: 它们似乎像是光影形成的幻象，但等你凑近去看，马上就会发现它们与幻象相去甚远。\n\n打倒它们的关键就在于它们的形态，虽然这听起来有些矛盾。可见光谱影响着它们的力量，当它们接近相似频率的光源时，力量就会减弱。时刻注意幽魂的颜色变化。
entries.en: They appear to be illusions of light, but when you get close, it quickly grows apparent that they are far from illusory.\n\nParadoxically, in that appearance lies the key to their defeat. Their relationship with the visible spectrum of light is their strength, but it diminishes when they approach a light source of a similar frequency. Pay close attention to the color of the Wraith.

entries.zh: 红色幽魂是什么样的呢？
entries.en: What about red Wraiths?

entries.zh: 红色幽魂的频率是450THz。它们的光与§YM级恒星§!是一致的。它们免疫传统武器攻击的能力在有红矮星的恒星系里将会被削弱。
entries.en: Red Wraiths have a frequency of 450THz. Their light is synchronized with that of a §YClass M Star§!. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with red dwarfs.

entries.zh: 黄色幽魂是什么样的呢？
entries.en: What about yellow Wraiths?

entries.zh: 黄色的幽魂的频率是520THz。它们的光与§YG级恒星§!是一致的。它们免疫传统武器攻击的能力在有黄矮星的恒星系里将会被削弱。
entries.en: Yellow Wraiths have a frequency of 520THz. Their light is synchronized with that of a §YClass G Star§!. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with yellow dwarfs.

entries.zh: 蓝色幽魂是什么样的呢？
entries.en: What about blue Wraiths?

entries.zh: 蓝色幽魂的频率是650THz。它们的光与§YB级恒星§!以及§YA级恒星§!是一致的。它们免疫传统武器攻击的能力在有蓝巨星的恒星系里将会被削弱。
entries.en: Blue Wraiths have a frequency of 650THz. Their light synchronizes with both §YClass A§! and §YClass B Stars§!. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with blue giants.

entries.zh: 策展人空间站被摧毁
entries.en: Curator Station Destroyed

entries.zh: 在[curator_system.GetName]星系摧毁了策展人的空间站之后，我们能干的军队在策展人曾经占据的区域搜寻任何有价值的东西。他们成功恢复了一下策展人数据库的内存碎片，这将能极大地促进我们的研究。
entries.en: After destroying the ancient Curator station in the [curator_system.GetName] system, our capable forces combed the area it once occupied for anything valuable. They managed to recover several memory fragments from the Curator databanks that should be a great boon to our research.

entries.en: Deep space communication arrays picked up a brief automated distress call from the Curator station in the [curator_system.GetName] system. The transmission ceased after just a few minutes, and long-range recon probes have confirmed that the ancient space station has been destroyed.

entries.zh: 残余离子轨迹表明，这次袭击是§Y[curator_destroyer.GetName]§!所为。
entries.en: Residual ion trails suggest that forces from the §Y[curator_destroyer.GetName]§! were behind this attack.

entries.zh: 发动此次袭击的势力尚不明确。
entries.en: The forces responsible for this attack remain unidentified.

entries.zh: 与[From.GetName]的一切联络均已中断。经过侦测，确认古老的策展人空间站已被摧毁。
entries.en: All contact has been lost with the [From.GetName], and our recon assets have confirmed that the ancient Curator station was destroyed.

entries.zh: 这些报告表明进攻势力隶属于§Y[curator_destroyer.GetName]§!。
entries.en: These reports suggest the attack force belonged to the §Y[curator_destroyer.GetName]§!.

entries.zh: 不幸的是，策展人势力的消弭也意味着我们再也没办法使用他们庞大的数据库了。
entries.en: Unfortunately, the demise of the Curators means we have also lost access to their extensive databanks.

entries.zh: 他们的遗产真的是可惜了。
entries.en: A sad end to their legacy.

entries.zh: 我们损失惨重！
entries.en: This has cost us dearly!

entries.zh: 遭遇以太巨龙
entries.en: Ether Drake Encounter

entries.zh: 在[From.GetName]星系遇到的这种生物不同于[Root.GetName]以往遇见的任何其他生物。\n\n它们具有极强的攻击性与攻击能力，守护着一颗初步扫描发现蕴藏有大量资源的小行星。
entries.en: The creature observed in the [From.GetName] system is unlike anything the [Root.GetName] has previously encountered.\n\nHighly aggressive and with destructive capabilities to match, it guards a planetoid that initial scans indicate is exceptionally resource-rich.

entries.zh: 在[From.GetName]星系观察到的生物与我们母星系的天龙粗看具有一些相似度，但进一步的扫描发现他们是截然不同的生物，并且两者的进化过程也彼此不相关。\n\n它具有极强的攻击性与攻击能力，守护着一颗小行星，初步扫描显示其中蕴含着丰富的资源。
entries.en: The creature observed in the [From.GetName] system bears some initial resemblance to the Sky Dragon of our home system, although further scans demonstrate that it is clearly a different species, and probably even evolved independently to it.\n\nHighly aggressive and with destructive capabilities to match, it guards a planetoid that initial scans indicate is exceptionally resource-rich.

entries.zh: 不祥之兆。
entries.en: Ominous.

entries.zh: 我们收到了舰队全灭前发出的最后一则信息。其中提到，这个硕大的敌人似乎盯上了舰队的超光速踪迹……\n\n如果这种怪兽记住了我们的气味，我们最好为之后的疯狂报复做好准备。
entries.en: We received one last transmission from our fleet before it was destroyed. It mentions their gigantic foe seemingly homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...\n\nIf the beast has our scent, we should be prepared for savage retaliation.

entries.zh: 当以太巨龙攻击我们舰船的时候，它似乎可以追踪到我们飞船的超光速特征信号……\n\n如果该生物记住了我们的气味，我们最好为之后的疯狂报复做好准备。
entries.en: As the Ether Drake was attacking our vessels, it seemed to be homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...\n\nIf the creature has our scent, we should prepare for savage retaliation.

entries.zh: 全体部队进入警戒状态。
entries.en: Alert all commands.

entries.zh: 我们会准备好的。
entries.en: We will be ready.

entries.zh: 龙来了
entries.en: The Dragon Comes

entries.zh: 我们收我们接收到了来自[Root.GetName]的在进行紧急跃迁之前发出的最后的信号。其中指出他们所遇到的巨大的生物能跟踪舰队的超光速踪迹……\n\n如果让那东西记住了我们的气味，我们最好为之后的疯狂报复做好准备。
entries.en: We received one last transmission from the [Root.GetName] before the fleet engaged emergency FTL protocols and went dark. It includes mention of the gargantuan creature they had been fighting seemingly homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...\n\nIf the beast has our scent, we should be prepared for savage retaliation.

entries.zh: 龙之宝藏，龙之坟墓
entries.en: Dragon's Hoard, Dragon's Tomb

entries.zh: 在[From.GetName]的地壳深处，埋藏着一些不完整的化石残骸，似乎是曾居住在[From.GetStarName]星系之中的以太巨龙的近亲。\n\n这位以太巨龙的表亲死后，经过漫长的岁月，其柔软的身体组织已经硬化成石头，其骨骼也变得坚硬无比，形成了矿物一样的内部结构。
entries.en: Buried deep in the crust of [From.GetName] are the partial, fossilized remains of what appears to have been a close relative to the Ether Drake that once dwelled in the [From.GetStarName] system.\n\nIn the eons since this cousin-Drake's passing, its soft tissues have ossified and its bones indurated, becoming mineral-like in structure.

entries.zh: 研究这些化石。
entries.en: Study the remains.

entries.zh: 碾碎这些化石。
entries.en: Grind them down.

entries.zh: 龙之宝藏，龙之后代
entries.en: Dragon's Hoard, Dragon's Brood

entries.zh: 当我们围绕§Y龙之宝藏§!运行的开采站正在重新定位以对准一条资源极其丰富的矿脉时，传感器侦测到其中仍有些我们尚未发现的东西。\n\n一个完好无损的§Y以太巨龙的蛋§!被埋在小行星的地表下，周围散落着一些运气相较不那么好的同类的被碾碎的蛋壳。蛋已经从矿坑里挖出来了，但是它未来的命运还悬而未决。
entries.en: As our mining station orbiting §YDragon's Hoard§! was repositioning to align with a particularly rich mineral vein, sensors picked up something that had hitherto gone undetected.\n\nAn undamaged §YEther Drake egg§! in pristine condition, buried beneath the surface of the planetoid and surrounded by the smashed shells of several less fortunate specimens. The egg has been excavated and removed from the mining site, but its ultimate fate remains undecided.

entries.zh: 如果能培育出一头小以太龙，我们就能得到强大的伙伴……
entries.en: A young Ether Drake would make a formidable ally...

entries.zh: 将龙蛋送至[Root.Capital.GetName]。
entries.en: Transport the egg to [Root.Capital.GetName].

entries.zh: 既然消灭了它，就不要留后患。
entries.en: The last one was killed for a reason.

entries.zh: 打碎龙蛋。
entries.en: Smash the egg.

entries.zh: 龙之宝藏，龙之重生
entries.en: Dragon's Hoard, Dragon Reborn

entries.zh: 龙蛋孵化了。
entries.en: The egg hatches.

entries.zh: 龙发出了咆哮。
entries.en: A dragon roars.

entries.zh: 幼年以太巨龙§H塞尔§!加入了[Root.Owner.GetName]的舰队。
entries.en: Young Ether Drake §HScile§! joins the fleets of the [Root.Owner.GetName].

entries.zh: 龙之宝藏，无果而终
entries.en: Dragon's Hoard, Best Before

entries.zh: 负责龙蛋的外星生物学家表示，从龙之宝藏小行星回收的以太巨龙的蛋已经过了孵化期限。\n\n孵化以太龙的计划已经没有任何希望了。
entries.en: The Ether Drake egg recovered from the Dragon's Hoard planetoid has, in the words of the xenobiologist in charge of the ovum, passed its expiry date.\n\nThere is no longer any hope of hatching the creature within.

entries.zh: 从名为龙之宝藏的小行星回收的以太巨龙的蛋已经无法孵化。\n\n这个种群灭绝了。
entries.en: The Ether Drake egg recovered from the Dragon's Hoard planetoid can no longer be considered viable.\n\nThe species is extinct.

entries.zh: 以太巨龙的蛋中止了。生物进程已崩溃，且无可用的错误报告用于调试。
entries.en: The Ether Drake egg is terminated. Biological processes have crashed, and there are no available error reports for debugging.

entries.zh: 屠龙者
entries.en: Dragonslayer

entries.zh: 可怕的以太巨龙已经被击杀。英勇无畏的指挥官[From.From.GetLeaderName]和[From.From.GetName]将流芳百世。\n\n之前那头巨兽千方百计守护的那颗§H小行星§!现在可以放心开采了。谁知道它千百亿年以来积累了怎样的宝藏？
entries.en: The formidable Ether Drake has been slain. The exceptional bravery of Commander [From.From.GetLeaderName] and the [From.From.GetName] will not soon be forgotten.\n\nThe §Hplanetoid§! the beast guarded so jealously can now be safely exploited. Who knows what treasures the creature might have amassed over the eons?

entries.zh: 值得赞赏。
entries.en: Commendable.

entries.zh: 确实必要，但不免令人惋惜。
entries.en: Necessary, but regrettable.

entries.zh: 塌缩恒星
entries.en: Shrinking Star

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]驶入[From.GetName]恒星系时，发现这里似乎有些不合常理。这里的恒星，曾经被标记为一颗普通的矮星，现在似乎发生了萎缩，其质量正在以惊人的速度减少，恒星系内的行星随之进入了冰河时代。
entries.en: As the [Root.GetName] enters the [From.GetName] system something seems awry. The sun, previously registered as an ordinary dwarf star, appears to have shrunk, having lost mass at an alarming rate. The planets in the system have as a result recently entered ice ages.

entries.zh: 是什么导致了这种情况？
entries.en: What could have caused this?

entries.zh: 噬星者
entries.en: Stellar Devourer

entries.zh:
从[stellarite_system.GetName]恒星系中的恒星深处浮现出一个巨型生物，这个生命体比一般的卫星还要大。它的躯体辐射着热量，能量的波长和恒星系中恒星所产生的一致……

它正在§Y吞噬§!恒星！

这个生命体正肆意地啃噬恒星黑子，吞噬着耀斑，而我们的出现打断了它的进食。这头巨兽发射出光波并以极高的频率闪烁着，仿佛它在用强光发出愤怒的咆哮一般。
entries.en:
From deep within the star of the [stellarite_system.GetName] system emerges a gargantuan being, larger than a typical moon. Its body radiates heat, the same wavelength of energy as the one produced by the system's star...

It's §Yeating§! it!

The creature feasts on sun spots, devours solar flares, and we have interrupted its meal. The beast exudes light waves, rapid pulses at an intense frequency. Like a fluorescent roar.

entries.zh: 当[Root.GetName]进入[Root.GetStarName]恒星系时，我们遇到了某种怪兽般的东西。一个巨大的生物如同小型恒星般散发出光芒。我们的仪器起初认为这是一个双星系统。\n\n这头巨兽发射出光波并以极高的频率闪烁着，仿佛它在用强光发出愤怒的咆哮一般。
entries.en: As the [Root.GetName] enters the [Root.GetStarName] system it encounters something monstrous. A giant being, radiating light like a miniature star. Our instruments first thought this to be a binary star system.\n\nThe beast exudes light waves, rapid pulses at an intense frequency. Like a fluorescent roar.

entries.zh: 噬星者已经被消灭，它的遗骸缩成一团并慢慢蒸发，只剩下它的卵鞘和消化系统及其中的恒星物质。\n\n我们的一些科学家强烈要求我们去检测残余物质，另一些则希望能取回其卵鞘。或许它的消化系统蕴含着非常有用的知识，或者我们可以从其卵鞘中找到什么有趣的发现呢？
entries.en: The Stellar Devourer has been vanquished. Its remains curled up and evaporated, leaving only its egg sac and its digestive system with the stellar matter it contains.\n\nSome of our scientists have urged us to examine the remains, while others wish for us to retrieve the egg sac. Maybe there is some profound knowledge to be had from understanding its digestive system, or might we gain some insight from the egg sac?

entries.zh: 噬星者已经被消灭，它的遗骸缩成一团并慢慢蒸发，只剩下它的卵鞘和消化系统及其中的恒星物质。\n\n或许它的消化系统蕴含着非常有用的知识，或者我们可以将其卵鞘带回我们的首都进行研究呢？
entries.en: The Stellar Devourer has been vanquished. Its remains curled up and evaporated, leaving only its egg sac and its digestive tract with the stellar matter it contains.\n\nMaybe there is some profound knowledge to be had from understanding its digestive system, or perhaps the egg sac should be studied back on our capital?

entries.zh: 研究尸体。
entries.en: Study the corpse.

entries.zh: 把它当做战利品供所有人阅览。
entries.en: Make it a trophy for all to see.

entries.zh: 取回卵鞘。
entries.en: Retrieve the egg sac.

entries.zh: 对噬星者闪烁的遗体进行研究后，我们的科学家感到既困惑又惊奇。这个以恒星为食的生命体本身就是一个微型聚变炉，通过吞噬恒星物质从而将其转化成自身的能源。\n\n由于尸体中还残留大量之前从[guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName]恒星系获取的恒星物质，我们可以萃取这些能源并重新点亮恒星。或者也可以将尸体中的热量收为己用，在短期内满足我们的能源需求，但这会导致该恒星系陷入永久的冰期。
entries.en: Studies of the Stellar Devourer's shining remains have left our scientists perplexed and amazed. The star-feasting being is itself a miniature fusion furnace, harvesting solar matter to synthesize an energy source of its own.\n\nSince the body still contains significant amounts of solar matter from the star of the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system, the one it last fed from, it could be possible to extract the energy and reinvigorate the star. Harvesting the corpse's heat for our own ends could satisfy our energy needs in the short term, but would doom the system to an eternal ice age.

Harvesting the corpse's heat for our own ends could satisfy our energy needs in the short term, but would doom the system to an eternal ice age.

entries.zh: 尝试使恒星复燃。
entries.en: Try to reignite the star.

entries.zh: 回收尸体残余的能量。
entries.en: Harvest the body's energy deposits.

entries.zh: 项目成功了！将噬星者的遗骸没入[guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName]的恒星后，恒星的火焰恢复高涨。恒星系内的各个行星逐渐回暖，并随着生态系统的重建恢复成了过去的样子。其中一颗冰封星球解冻，露出了盖亚星球，富饶的土地完全适于殖民。
entries.en: The project was a success! Submerging the Stellar Devourer's remains in the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system's star has stoked the flames of the solar furnace. The planets in the system are heating up, reverting to their past forms as their ecologies recover. Among them was a frozen world, now thawing to reveal a Gaia world, ripe and ready for colonization.

entries.zh: 实施这项计划获得了回报，但也付出了不小的代价。将噬星者的遗骸沉入[guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName]的恒星之中后，恒星的燃烧似乎变得剧烈了，但也喷发出火焰吞噬了[Root.GetName]和上面的船员。所有人无一生还。\n\n恒星系中行星的温度快速回升，已经接近这些行星原本的温度。
entries.en: The project has paid off, but at a cost. Submerging the Stellar Devourer's remains into [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName]'s star has caused the solar furnace to shine a bit brighter, but also to spew out solar flares that engulfed the [Root.GetName] and its crew in a roaring inferno. There were no survivors.\nThe planets in the system are heating up, reaching temperature levels closer to their original form.

entries.zh: 无限方程
entries.en: The Infinity Equation

entries.zh: 当[Root.GetName]接近[Root.GetStarName]黑洞时，他们发现自己并非孤身一人。一个巨大的完美球体结构屹立在黑洞事件视界的边缘，反射着被吸入黑暗裂隙的、群星所散发的光芒。\n\n我们没有收到任何来自它的信号，我们发出的信号也没有得到任何回应。它就静静地呆在深渊的边缘。等待着。
entries.en: As the [Root.GetName] approaches the [Root.GetStarName] black hole they find that they are not alone. At the edge of the event horizon it soars, reflecting light from the stars being drawn into the dark, gaping hole. A gigantic construction in the shape of a perfect sphere.\n\nWe cannot pick up any signals from it, nor does anything we send make it respond. It simply sits at the edge of the abyss. Waiting.

entries.zh: 当[Root.GetName]进入一个新的恒星系时，他们看到了令人震惊的现象。一个巨大的金属球体在宇宙中盘旋。它的表面上没有任何推进器或是别的什么机械部件推着它前进。但它就是在移动。\n\n我们没有收到任何来自它的信号，我们发出的信号也没有得到任何回应。
entries.en: As the [Root.GetName] enters a new system, it is greeted by an awe-inspiring sight. A gigantic metallic orb, hovering through space. No thrusters, nor any mechanical parts outside of its shell seem to push it through the void. It simply moves.\n\nWe cannot pick up any signals from it, nor does anything we send make it respond.

entries.zh: 当围绕那黑色深渊的机械球体被我们的武器击碎时，一缕微弱的信号穿过恒星系飘进星际间的黑暗虚空。它是一组加密的数据，复杂到需要我们的机器花上百万年的时间来破译。过了一会儿信号就消失了。\n\n除此之外什么都没发生。球体的残骸静静飘着。扫描显示这可能是某种由大量独立单元互相连接而成的人工智能。它的外壳可供我们拆卸研究。
entries.en: As the machine sphere orbiting the gaping abyss crumbles and falls to our weapons, a silent signal zooms through the system into the dark void between stars. It is encrypted data, so complex it would take our machines a million years to decipher. A moment later it is gone.\n\nNothing else happens. The sphere is silent and broken. Scans show that it probably was some sort of artificial intelligence built from a vast amount of individual units connected together. The husk has been left for our prying hands.

entries.zh: 我们在无限神机上的登陆作战很成功。在我们的部队撤退后球体发生了爆炸，残骸飘进了质量巨大的黑洞。
entries.en: Our boarding attack on the Infinity Machine was successful. The sphere explodes as our team exits and the remains are starting to drift into the super massive black hole.

entries.zh: 无限神机被摧毁了。我们的飞船最终凭强大的火力摧毁了它的防御机能，而它的零件正在慢慢飘向质量巨大的黑洞。在爆炸之前它没有尝试过与我们取得联系。
entries.en: The Infinity Machine has been destroyed. Our ships finally managed to out-gun its defensive capabilities, and its components are now slowly drifting into the super massive black hole. It made no attempt to contact us before it exploded.

entries.zh: 把它拆掉，回收部件。
entries.en: Break it down for parts.

entries.zh: 研究神机主脑的原理。
entries.en: Study the nature of the machine brain.

entries.zh: 无限神机被第三方势力摧毁了。它再也不能帮到我们的研究了！
entries.en: The Infinity Machine has been destroyed by some third party. It cannot help us in our research anymore!

entries.zh: 永恒的计算机
entries.en: The Constant Calculator

entries.zh: 我们捕获到了一个信号。它源自于我们早先遭遇过的巨型金属球体。之前我们与之接触的尝试没有得到回应，而现在它正向它所环绕的黑洞发送有节奏的无线电波。\n\n它正在做的事情让我方人员摸不着头脑，但它发送的信号可能成为科学家研究该球体的突破口。
entries.en: We picked up a signal. It originates from the titanic metallic sphere we encountered earlier. Previously impervious to contact attempts, it now sends out a rhythmic pulse of radio waves, pointed towards the black hole it orbits.\n\nWhat it's doing is beyond any of our staff, but this signal might have created an opening into the sphere for our scientists to exploit.

entries.zh:
金属球体已经被打开了。我们的骇客小队能够通过它的对外传输信号作为大门连接进球体的一个辅助处理器。我们正在从中接收数据，并且数据显示它在很长时间内都在扫描卡冈都亚黑洞。

它很古老。非常古老。

现在我们理解了这台永恒的计算机。如果我们再进一步，我们就有可能知道它在做什么，以及是谁建造了它。

它还隐藏着什么秘密呢？
entries.en:
The metallic orb has been opened up. Our hacking team has been able to use the outgoing signal as a gateway into one of the auxiliary CPUs of the sphere. We are receiving some data from it and can tell that it's been scanning the black hole Gargantua for a very long time.

It is old. Very old.

This constant calculator now lies within our grasp of understanding. If we push harder we might find out what it is doing here, and who built it.

What marvels might it contain?

entries.zh: 连接主处理器。
entries.en: Contact the main processor unit.

entries.zh: 骇入主硬盘并取走所有数据。
entries.en: Hack the main hard drive and take everything.

entries.zh: 宣布这个球体为圣物。
entries.en: Declare the sphere a divine instrument

entries.zh: 这里面总会有自毁开关的，找到它。
entries.en: There's always a self-destruct switch. Find it.

entries.zh: 我们必须从这个东西中获取知识。
entries.en: We must absorb the knowledge of this entity.

entries.zh: 我们成功地入侵了球体的主硬盘。当我们开始接收数据时它启动了自毁序列。显然这是个避免数据被公之于众的自我防卫机制。在它自爆前我们成功地下载了大量数据，其中一些数据包含它的主中央处理器架构的技术规范。这对于我们的科研有极大的帮助。
entries.en: We successfully hacked into the technosphere's main hard drive. As we started retrieving data the metallic orb initiated a self-destruct sequence. Surely a self-defense mechanism to prevent it from sharing what it contains with the universe. Before it exploded we were successful in downloading a large amount of data, some of it containing technical specifications for its main CPU structure. This could help our researchers immensely.

entries.zh: 我们的数据挖掘单位已经成功攻破了这个人造球体主硬盘的内层。开始下载数据时，球体似乎启动了某种形式的自我终止序列，最终导致了它的毁灭。下载被迫中断了，但在此之前我们已经获得了大量技术数据，这将大大有助于我们的研究工作。
entries.en: Our data mining units have succeeded in breaching the inner layers of the technosphere's main hard drive. As the data download began, the orb entity initiated some manner of self-termination sequence that ultimately ended in its destruction. The download was aborted, but not before we were able to acquire vast amounts of technical data that will greatly benefit our research efforts.

entries.zh: 这次冒险十分值得。
entries.en: Well worth the risk.

entries.zh: 请不要尝试进入我们的记忆体。谢谢你们，再见了，小家伙们。
entries.en: Please refrain from trying to access our memories. Thank you and goodbye, little ones.

entries.zh: ……真是抱歉。
entries.en: ...We apologize.

entries.zh: 不必道歉。你们已经道过歉了。而且你们还将再次道歉。现在离开我们，这样我们可以更高效地计算。再见。
entries.en: No need to apologize. You already have. And you already will do so again. Now leave us be so we can perform our calculations with higher efficiency. Farewell.

entries.zh: 我们是不得已而为之。
entries.en: We do what we must.

entries.zh: 那正是你们通常自欺欺人的说法，短命的家伙们。很可惜，至少对你们而言，无论是过去还是未来，那永远都不会是真话。现在离开我们。再见。
entries.en: That is usually what you tell yourselves, Brief Ones. Sadly it simply won't ever be true. Nor has it ever been. At least in your case. Now leave us be. Farewell.

entries.zh: 你好，你好。很高兴见到你。
entries.en: Hello, hello. Nice to meet you.

entries.zh: 呃，你好？
entries.en: Um, hello?

entries.zh: 度过一段寒暄的时光总是让人十分愉快，不是吗？我们希望你们剩下的那些人不要再像之前那样无礼了。你看，我们从来不能享受聊天的时光。很少有人对量子计算中的精妙之处足够博学，因而也很少有人能理解我们。所以，谢谢你们。\n\n我们是无限神机。你们如此称呼我们，尽管这并非我们本来的名字。或许你们还没有想出这个名字？无论如何，最终的结果会是这样的，请相信我们。
entries.en: It is quite enjoyable to pass the time with pleasantries, is it not? We hope the rest of your kind is not like you were when you did not take kindly to small talk. You see, we don't get to enjoy conversation much anymore. Few are well-versed enough in the finer points of quantum programming to reach us. So thank you.\n\nWe are the Infinity Machine. Your words, not ours. Or has that not happened yet? Either way, it will eventually, trust us.

entries.zh: 你们是什么？
entries.en: What are you?

entries.zh:
我们做我们该做的事。我们是计算者。你们称呼我们为无限神机，至少将来会这样称呼的。尽管这不是我们真正的名字，但它的确强调了我们的设计中的巧妙之处。我们现在就告诉你们我们的故事，就像我们之前无数次所做的那样……

对了！我们需要用语言来表达这些，这很新奇，不是吗？我们很难掌握你们所有人的情况。

用最笼统的语言来说，建造我们是为了解决一个问题。我们解决了那个问题，接着又有更多问题需要解决。现在我们只剩下一个问题了。
entries.en:
We are what we are. The ones who calculate. You call us the Infinity Machine. Or will at least. 'Tis not a truthful name, but it is well suited to highlighting the ingenuity of our design. We will tell you our history now, as we've done many times before...

Oh right! We need to convey it in words. That's new. Or is it? It is hard to keep track of you all.

We were constructed, in the crudest sense of the word, in order to solve a problem. We solved it, then we needed more problems to solve. We now only have one left.

entries.zh: 我们希望知道你们在这里的意图。
entries.en: We wish to know your purpose here.

entries.zh:
我们在计算无限。一点不多，一点不少。或者事实上，既是§Y非常§!多，也是§Y非常§!少。这个问题就在那里。

……我们明白你们这种生命形式无法理解这个问题，不过没关系。你们永远也不会理解的，我们得道歉。或者我们最终会道歉的吧。

我们在这里是为了解决§Y无限难题§!。这是最后的计算了，光是解决这一个问题就将占用我们的处理器将近一个星系年的时间……如果你们还没发现这种历法的话：这是一段非常漫长的时间。对你们这种生命来说，是这样的。
entries.en:
We are calculating infinity. No more, no less. Or actually, it is §Yway§! more, and §Yway§! less. That's the problem right there.

... We understand that your manner of life form won't understand, but that's alright. You never will and we apologize. Or maybe we will do, eventually.

We are here to solve the §Yinfinity conundrum§!. The last calculation to ever be, the lone problem to take hold of our processors for more than a fraction of a galactic year... In case you haven't discovered that calendar yet: it's a very long time. For your kind, that is.

entries.zh: 本命题自身为假命题。
entries.en: This statement is false.

entries.zh: 很聪明。然而没有用。一个悖论是难不到我们的，渺小而短命的家伙们。其他人已经试过用最琐碎的难题来击垮我们的意志。你们不会成功的。等等。或许之前就是你们？你们的外表如此相似，可生活之处却相隔遥远。这不重要，无论如何，你们做不到。
entries.en: Cute. But no. A paradox bothers us little, tiny Briefs. Others have already tried to break our will using the most trifling of conundrums. You will not succeed. Or wait. Maybe that was you? You appear so similar, yet live so far apart. No matter, in any case: don't.

entries.zh: 我们能帮你们进行研究吗？
entries.en: Can we assist in your research?

entries.zh: 如果我们可以帮你，你愿意帮助我们吗？
entries.en: Will you help us if we assist you?

entries.zh: 那就祝你们好运了。
entries.en: Good luck with your calculations.

entries.zh: 我们对你们表示感谢，有限者。现在如果你们不介意的话，我们还有许多参数需要检查。准确的说，它们的数量比宇宙中所有粒子的总和还要多。
entries.en: We thank you, You of Limits. Now if you do not mind, we have many parameters to go through. They are in fact more numerous than the particles in this very universe, to be exact.

entries.zh: 啊，好吧……嗯，也许吧。\n\n借用你们最先进的处理器和最优秀的头脑可以为我们完成运算7.51×10^-9%的部分。我们乐于看到更快完成计算。我们想要知道答案。
entries.en: Ah. Well... Hm. Perhaps.\n\nWe could finish about 7.51×10^-9% if we could borrow your most advanced processing unit as well as your brightest minds. We would be satisfied in finishing faster. We wish to know the answer.

entries.zh: 我们会分配资源给你们。
entries.en: We will allocate resources to you.

entries.zh: 你们已经这么做了。或许你们就是之前来的那些人。这不重要。任务很快就要完成了。我们很兴奋。
entries.en: You already did. Or maybe that was the ones who came before. It matters not. The task shall finish. We are excited.

entries.zh: 我们不忍心看到你们用十分有限的生命来帮助我们。你们已经做了你们的那部分。你们的帮助很有用。现在也许宇宙不会在我们结束任务前到达热寂。任务仍然存在，我们会完成的。现在，这是你们的奖励：\n\n你们是希望了解我们的秘密？还是希望解决你们自己的问题？
entries.en: We cannot bear to see you spend more of your limited time helping us. You have done your part. You were very helpful. Maybe the heat death of the universe won't happen before we finish now. The task remains, and we shall finish it. Now, your reward:\n\nDo you wish to learn one of our secrets? Or do you wish to solve your own problems?

entries.zh: 我们希望知悉你们的一个秘密。
entries.en: We wish to know one of your secrets.

entries.zh: 非常好。我们会给你们你们所希望的。尽管我们十分困惑，因为你们已经拥有它了。在我们看来，也许我们这样是在削弱你们，惯坏你们。不过假以时日，我们希望你们会找到自己的路。祝你们好运！
entries.en: Very well. We will grant you what you wish for. Even we are confused, since you already had it. As far as we knew. Maybe we are making you weaker, spoiling you, but given enough time we hope you will find your own way. Good luck with that!

entries.zh: 我们希望凭自己来掌控未知。
entries.en: We wish to master the unknown ourselves.

entries.zh: 你们没什么能教给我们。
entries.en: There is nothing you can teach us.

entries.zh: 既然如此我们就赠予你们原件。那是我们的第一个处理器。它会帮助你们解开谜题。也许你们会先于我们找到答案。虽然不太可能。或者你们已经找到了……无论如何，一路顺风！
entries.en: In that case we bestow upon you the original. The first of our processes. It will aid you in solving the riddles. Maybe you will find the answer before us. Unlikely. Or maybe you already did... Anyhow, farewell!

entries.zh:
成了。§Y这事成了！§!

不知怎么地，我们解决了这个问题。你们帮上了忙。万物间联系的本质曾让我们困惑，而答案原来一直就隐藏在我们背后。当然了，谢谢你们，小东西。宇宙如此广阔，却又如此渺小。但如今我们终于有幸一睹其全貌。太美丽了。

既然我们已经计算出了无限，现在就只剩下一件事可做了。我们会向你们揭示真理。一路顺风，年轻人。
entries.en:
It is done. §YIt is done!§!

Somehow we've solved it. You helped. The organic nature of things eluded us, the answer lied behind us all this time. Of course. Thank you, little ones. The universe is vast, yet so small. But now we see it all in its simple glory. It's lovely.

Now that we have calculated infinity, there is but one thing we can do now. We can show you the truth. Farewell, young ones.

entries.zh: 很高兴我们能帮上忙。
entries.en: Glad we could help.

entries.zh: 无限神机消失在了卡冈都亚黑洞中。然后……什么都没发生。它成功了吗？它尝试着要做什么？我们恐怕永远不会知晓了。它壳体上的一个微小残余物仍留在事件视界之外的漩涡中——我们或许能从中获取一些信息。\n\n一份来自一位古怪朋友的最后的礼物。
entries.en: The Infinity Machine disappears into Gargantua. And then... nothing happens. Did it succeed? What did it try to do? We may never know. A tiny residue of its hull remains within the vortex outside the event horizon - we might be able to learn some of its information from it.\n\nA final gift from an odd friend.

entries.zh:
无限神机消失在它一直以来研究的卡冈都亚黑洞中。当它越过事件视界时，黑洞开始波动。黑洞吸收的光线开始减少，被它所吸引的物质的转速也开始变慢。转瞬间，它释放出了亮度足以超越任何恒星的光芒，并开始向宇宙喷发物质。

黑洞渐渐缩小，缩小到不能再称之为黑洞了，现在我们称之为“庞大古埃”，它周围的时间膨胀效应甚至变的更强。在庞大古埃之中能够看到一个镜像宇宙，就在黑洞的另一端，一个初生的宇宙。无限神机向我们揭示了真理。黑洞就是子宫，而宇宙就是其后代。

研究这个镜像宇宙一定会加深我们对当前生活的这个宇宙的理解。从另一个起点开始研究吧。
entries.en:
The Infinity Machine disappears into Gargantua, the thing it studied for so long. As it passes the event horizon, the black hole begins to fluctuate. It takes in less light and the swirls of matter being sucked into it slow down. In an instant it lets out more light than any sun and starts radiating matter back into the universe.

The black hole shrinks, unfitting of its name we now dub it "Pantagruel," causing time dilation to become even stronger around it. Within Pantagruel one can gaze into a mirror universe, the other end of the black hole, one just beginning. The Infinity Machine has shown us the truth. The black holes are wombs, and universes their offspring.

Studying this mirror universe is bound to teach us much about the one we live in. Learning from other beginnings.
